stats: A statistic such as a mean, a variance or a correlation is computed on a whole table at once. This page lists the statistics of the machine learning part of the library: covariance and correlation, moments, the exponentially weighted mean and variance, rolling windows, the rolling median and the shrunk covariance.
preprocessing: Before a model sees the data, the table is rescaled, some columns are dropped, the joint records are turned into velocities and the text is turned into numbers. Each class reads the whole table with `fit` and applies the result with `transform`.
linear: A linear model predicts a number, or the probability of a class, as a weighted sum of the features. Here the weights are found on the whole table: by one linear solve for the regression, by Newton steps for the logistic model, and as a posterior distribution for the Bayesian regression.
optim: An optimiser moves the weights downhill on a loss. These classes take the gradient of the loss over the whole dataset and apply the update rule of the paper, step after step, so they can minimise any loss whose gradient you can write.
bayes: A naive Bayes classifier counts how often each feature value goes with each class and turns the counts into probabilities. Here the counts are taken over the whole table, with a small pseudo-count so that no probability is zero.
neighbors: A nearest-neighbour model answers a question about a new row by looking at the rows of the table that are closest to it: the most common class among them, or the average of their targets.
multiclass: A binary classifier answers yes or no. To choose among many classes, these strategies train several binary classifiers on the whole table and combine their answers: one against all the others, one for every pair of classes, or one for every bit of a codeword.
multioutput: Some problems have several targets at once, for example the position and the speed of a joint. These classes build one model per target, or a chain in which each model also sees the targets of the earlier links, or a chain that finds the most probable set of labels as a whole.
proba: A distribution summarises a sample in a few numbers. These classes keep the posterior of the Beta, Gaussian and Multinomial families: the prior counts plus the counts observed in the whole sample.
